facts.fact: Gauri's word about the Widow's Ladder comes on day 22 by a bound pair of runners from the Kuhl side, not a boy (revises F615).

The east bearing is a pencilled cairn-light bearing in Ila's field-book margin, never walked. The Shared Map carries the margin note 'East bearing, cairn-light, seen. Not walked. Not drawn.' Ila states 'I don't draw a way I haven't walked' to Kunal and publicly at the signing.
Day-35 test: Kunal fetches a sheet drying in the herders' fold, sixteen spans out, and feels no cold.
The Under-Cairn door is drawn on the Shared Map with 'Harish' written beside it in the hill hand.
Queen Sarala 'keeps your grandfather in a locked drawer for thirty-one winters' and, as the price of Ila's refusal, bars Ila from the royal archive's drawers for life.
Pell Orlan takes the Chief Surveyor's chair.
The queen is 62 and travels with eight bearers and two mules.
Rohan hears about Harish on day 18 in the Shilak post room, having stood three dawns at the cairn.
